precepts.text: All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes. That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. And when they come, we will show them how to get right.
precepts.point: News discussed in class: the hands of the civil rights era are being turned back right now. Memphis, one of the blackest cities in America, has been carved up by gerrymandering and parceled out to the outskirts of the state so that its people cannot win a congressional seat any more; it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers protesting that he was lawfully there. We frame the law by mischief is written for a reason. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and the churches that once organized the community are silent. Where is the Christian church on the front line while all of this is turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 and it is ruled suicide? The only ones crying aloud about it are the Israelites. The teaching stands: our people need to see the affliction for what it is, get their minds right, and get lined up on the right side before the decree brings forth.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” God returns to his place, and our people have to seek him, but they have to be afflicted first. That is how our people are. And the afflictions are just starting. We have been getting killed in the street by police, but that ain't it; that is only the prelude to what is about to happen.

Esau is turning back the hands of the civil rights era right now, and that is good, because black people trust in their oppression. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parcelled out to the outskirts of the state so no black man can win a congressional seat there anymore, and it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers, protesting that he was an elected official and lawfully there. White guilt is out the window. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and they need the affliction, to see the devil for who he is.

In Esther's day: “All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. Right now they are still confused about who the devil is.

The church that once organized the community and planned the votes is silent while the civil rights laws are turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 with their organs taken out and it is called suicide. The only ones crying out about it are the Israelites. So it is our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come with death before their eyes, we will show them what they are doing wrong and how to get right.

precepts.text: Gather yourselves together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger. If you are seeking righteousness, you are admitting you do not yet have it; you are walking in error and correcting it. So when you come to the house of learning and somebody shows you your error, do not leave mad; leaving means going back out to face the fierce anger unprepared.

An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers protesting that he was lawfully there. We frame the law by mischief is written for a reason. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and the churches that once organized the community are silent. Where is the Christian church on the front line while all of this is turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 and it is ruled suicide? The only ones crying aloud about it are the Israelites. The teaching stands: our people need to see the affliction for what it is, get their minds right, and get lined up on the right side before the decree brings forth.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Our people will cry earnestly when death is before their eyes, and Zephaniah says what to do before it comes: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” If you are seeking righteousness, you are admitting that you don't have it yet; you are walking in error and correcting it. So pray, Lord, show me where I am in error so I can fix it, so that when your decree brings forth I am lined up on the right side. That means when somebody is sent to tell you, this is wrong, you hear it and learn, because you don't want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

So when you come to the house of learning and somebody shows you your error, don't get mad and leave. Leaving means going back out there to face the fierce anger of God unprepared. While you are here, you are going to learn how to turn away from your sins.

As we see these afflictions happening, we know the judgment and the fierce anger of the Lord are coming. Our people are clueless about what is about to happen to them; in America we are so comfortable that hard living means cancelling Netflix. It is our job to warn them, and they have to be willing to listen and be gathered before the decree brings forth.

precepts.text: Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you.
precepts.point: Seeking his face means seeing in Revelation 1:14 that Christ looks like his people. The house, the car and the barbecue are Esau's way of life.

note.label: Latinos For Trump: Alien Vs. Predator

precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” Why do we have to get deported? So that we seek God early. A lot of our people think this is the American dream, this is what life is about: get a house, get a car, barbecue on the weekend, watch sports, send your kids to college. No, that is Esau's way of life. This is death, this is oppression, and the Most High has to afflict us to remind us that this is not our rest.

Micah says it: “Arise ye, and depart”. Separate yourself from these heathen nations, these strangers, the real aliens. “for this is not your rest”. You were not brought here on slave ships to be comfortable, to assimilate, or to be friends with these heathen nations. You see the betrayal time and time again when you make a league with the strangers. “Our necks are under persecution: we labour, and have no rest”: we work and we have to watch our backs for ICE agents who come to our places of business and our homes, arrest us and kidnap our children.

“because it is polluted”: wicked, evil, deceptive. Witchcraft is in this place, so bad that it has you bleaching your skin, blonding your hair, putting in contacts, starving yourself. “it shall destroy you”: it destroyed Sammy Sosa, Serena Williams, Lil' Kim. Those are the celebrities Esau upholds so our people look up to them and want to be like them. It is witchcraft to make a black man hate himself so much that he destroys his own face.

“even with a sore destruction.” Destruction is coming to this place; this kingdom is not going to last forever. We are in the last days, so we have to get our minds right and our spirits right. There is much work to be done, especially for you so-called Latinos: Judah has shown us the way, and now it is our turn. When you see a head of state like Nicolás Maduro kidnapped and his country's resources stolen, that is for you to wake up. Seek his face, and see in the scriptures that he looks just like us.

precepts.text: In their affliction they will seek me early.
precepts.point: He delivereth the poor in his affliction and openeth their ears in oppression. Affliction is the only time the people turn to God.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.” When our people are oppressed, God opens their ears. All the things Trump is doing, and ICE is doing in the streets and in the black community, are God opening your ears. For the last 60 years our people have been lost and confused, following the American dream and thinking America is about equal rights and opportunity. God said, no, this place is not your rest. So he turns up the oppression, because that is the only time we as a people turn to God: when bad things start happening to us.

Hosea says it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Until we acknowledge our offence and seek God's face.

In our affliction we will seek him early: before it is too late, before we die, before judgment comes. So God is allowing Trump to do these things in the black community with these ICE agents so that you will seek him. Our people are realizing that the American dream is exactly what it is, a dream, and that there is no such thing here as justice and equal rights. That is why judgment starts first with the house of God.

precepts.text: In their affliction they will seek me early; the oppression is used to wake the people up.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
Why would the Most High harden the rulers so they continue to oppress Israel? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The oppression is used to wake the people up. In the affliction the people will seek him early, acknowledge their offence and seek his face.

So in spiritual Egypt today he hardens the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom so they will not let Israel go, and the affliction drives the people to him. Pharaoh's hardened heart showed the signs of the Most High before Egypt; the hardened hearts of these rulers bring Israel back to seek his face.

precepts.text: I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.
precepts.point: The curse was to be cursed coming in and cursed going out, coming in from war and going out to war, and the same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said”. Our offence is leaving off the commandments to serve other gods, and the Most High has gone and returned to his place: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Judges is the record of that affliction beginning to come upon our people for turning our backs on the one true living God.

Look at us today: Black Lives Matter, hands up don’t shoot. We cannot stand before our enemies, so now we beg our enemies to see us as people, to see us as human. We wonder why we cannot get anywhere as a people: individual millionaires, yet no infrastructure, no farms enough to set up our own stores and feed ourselves, no distribution, no hospitals, no textiles, none of the things a nation needs to sustain a nation. The Most High stays in his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face; in our affliction we will seek him early.

precepts.text: In their affliction they will seek me early; affliction is how the Most High wakes his people up to repent.
precepts.point: The Most High is in control of everything, good and evil alike. Even affliction that comes on his people is his tactic to make them seek him and repent; nothing anybody does can alter the outcome he has already ordained, for he declared the end from the beginning.

note.label: Judges 14: An Occasion Against the Philistines

precepts.why: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” “at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel”: that affliction was the Most High’s own tactic to make his people seek him and repent. Affliction is how the Most High wakes his people up. And the same Lord who let the Philistines have dominion was now seeking an occasion against them through Samson. Good and evil alike are in his control: he afflicts to bring repentance, and he avenges his people when the time comes.

precepts.text: The Most High will return to his place till they acknowledge their offence and seek his face in their affliction; the afflicted people is Israel.
precepts.point: The afflicted people the Most High saves, but his eyes are upon the haughty to bring them down. The afflicted is Israel. He is David's lamp and lightens his darkness, for by the Most High David ran through a troop, a body of some two hundred men or more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The afflicted people is Israel.

David sang, “And the afflicted people thou wilt save: but thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them down.” Israel is the people the Most High leaves in affliction till they acknowledge their offence and seek his face, and it is the afflicted people he saves.

“For thou art my lamp, O Lord: and the Lord will lighten my darkness. For by thee I have run through a troop”: a troop is a body of some two hundred men or more.

precepts.text: The Most High says he will go and return to his place till we acknowledge our offense and seek his face; in our affliction we will seek him early.
precepts.point: This was done not just against Adam and Eve but against all their descendants, because we broke the commandments and turned our back on the Most High first, so our punishment was that God turned his back on us.

note.label: Job 34: God Renders to Every Man According to His Ways

precepts.why:
Job asks, “when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only”. The Most High tells us he did it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

He hid his face and turned his back on us until we acknowledge our offense and seek his face. We could not make him turn around; when he gives quietness, who can make trouble, and if the Lord shuts this kingdom down nobody can stop him. But in our affliction we seek him early.

This was done not just against Adam and Eve but against all their descendants, against a nation and not a man only, because we broke the commandments and turned our back on the Most High first. So our punishment was that God turned his back on us, till we acknowledge our offence and seek his face.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to His place until we acknowledge our offense and seek Him early in our affliction.
precepts.point: When the Most High is silent against us it is the same thing as Hosea: He withdraws and does not listen to our prayers until we seek His face.

note.label: Psalm 28: Be Not Silent To Me

precepts.why:
“Unto thee will I cry, O Lord my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.” When the Most High is silent against us, it is the same thing as Hosea: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

He withdraws and returns to His place, and does not listen to our prayers, until we acknowledge our offense and seek His face. In our affliction we seek Him early. That is why David cries, be not silent to me, and lifts up his hands toward the holy oracle.

precepts.text: The Most High will go and return to his place until they acknowledge their offence and seek his face; in their affliction they will seek him early.
precepts.point: Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High. This is Hosea 5:15; when affliction comes we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. Even people in the world call on the Lord when things go wrong, though he does not always hear them.

note.label: Psalm 42: Panting After God in the Midst of Affliction

precepts.why:
“Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God”. Hosea shows why the affliction comes and what it does: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The Most High goes and returns to his place until they acknowledge their offence and seek his face, and in their affliction they seek him early.

Punishment for sins drives you back to the Most High. When affliction comes, we go back to the Lord, and that is how the Lord gets us back. Even people in the world call on the Lord when things go wrong, though he does not always hear them. For David, cast down with a sword in his bones, the affliction is what turned him back to hope in God, “who is the health of my countenance, and my God.”

precepts.text: The Most High returns to his place until Israel acknowledges their offense and seeks his face in their affliction.
precepts.point: Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy holy spirit from me. The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High. Hosea shows what happens when he withdraws it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Most High returns to his place until Israel acknowledges their offence and seeks his face. In our affliction we seek him early. That is why David prays not to be cast away from his presence: being out of his presence is the affliction, and acknowledging the offence is the way back into it.

precepts.text: The Lord will return to His place until they acknowledge their offense and seek His face; in their affliction they will seek Him early.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
“When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God.” Hosea shows this is how the Lord works with us: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Lord returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face. In our affliction we seek him early. Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping his laws, statutes and commandments.

Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way he wants, and when he slays us we remember that God is our rock and the high God our redeemer.

precepts.text: In our afflictions we will seek Him early, so we cry daily to the Lord in repentance until He hear us.
precepts.point: His eye mourneth by reason of affliction; he has called daily upon the Most High and stretched out his hands unto Him. When the Lord turns His face from us, a lot of this stuff is relevant to us today, like the dead bodies laying in the streets of the great city.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
“Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: Lord, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.” Hosea shows why the affliction and the daily calling go together: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Lord goes back to his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face. In our afflictions we will seek him early, so we cry daily to the Lord in repentance until he hear us.

When the Lord turns his face from us, he lays us in the lowest pit, in darkness, and puts our acquaintance far from us. A lot of this stuff is relevant to us today, like the dead bodies laying in the streets of the great city. The way out is what Hosea says: acknowledge the offence, seek his face early, and keep calling daily.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to His place until we acknowledge our offense and seek His face; in our affliction we will seek Him early, so sometimes affliction is good for our people that we may seek the Lord.
precepts.point: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death and brake their bands asunder. He broke the gates of brass and cut the bars of iron in sunder, taking away our captivity.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses.” Hosea shows what has to happen first: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Most High returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence, the wrong we did in breaking God's laws, and seek his face. That is when he begins to save us, bringing us out of darkness and the shadow of death and breaking our bands in sunder.

“in their affliction they will seek me early.” So sometimes affliction is good for our people, that we may seek the Lord. Then he breaks the gates of brass and cuts the bars of iron in sunder, taking away our captivity.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to His place until they acknowledge their offense and seek His face; in affliction they will seek Him early. When things are good we do not focus on the Father; only when judgment comes do we consider our God.
precepts.point: When the Most High hides His face, that is where we are today. He promised that if we walk in all His ways He would be with us and fight our battles.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why:
“Hear me speedily, O Lord: my spirit faileth: hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.” “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” When the Most High hides his face, that is where we are today. He returns to his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face; in affliction we seek him early.

When things are good we do not focus on the Father; only when judgment comes do we consider our God. He promised that if we walk in all his ways he would be with us and fight our battles.

precepts.text: The Most High goes and returns to His place until Israel acknowledges its offence and seeks His face.
precepts.point: "And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city." He will fix what is broken; some already keep the laws in the fear of the Most High rather than waiting for affliction to seek Him.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

precepts.why:
“Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies”. He will ease Himself, turning His back and letting the nations go. Hosea says the same: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

The Most High goes and returns to His place until Israel acknowledges its offence and seeks His face. Then, instead of dealing with the other nations, He turns to deal with the nation of Israel: “I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin”, and He will “restore thy judges as at the first”. He will fix what is broken. In their affliction they will seek Him early, but some already keep the laws in the fear of the Most High rather than waiting for affliction to seek Him.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to his place until, in their affliction, the people seek him early.
precepts.point: The people turn not to him that smites them, neither do they seek the Lord of hosts.

note.label: Isaiah 9: For Unto Us a Child Is Born

precepts.why:
The people would not turn to him that smote them, and would not seek the Lord of hosts. Hosea shows what the Most High does with a people like that: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face”. He withdraws and leaves them to their affliction.

But the affliction has a purpose: “in their affliction they will seek me early.” The smiting in Isaiah 9:13 is meant to turn the people back to him, and when they will not turn, he returns to his place until the affliction makes them acknowledge their offence and seek his face.

precepts.text: He returns to His place until they acknowledge their offense and seek His face, and in their affliction they will seek Him early.
precepts.point: The houses thrown down by the mount and the sword would be filled with the dead bodies of men He slew in His anger, for He hid His face from the city for all their wickedness.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The Lord says of Jerusalem, “for all whose wickedness I have hid my face from this city.” Hosea tells how long he hides it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

He returns to his place until they acknowledge their offense and seek his face. The houses thrown down and filled with the dead bodies of men slain in his anger and his fury are the affliction, and in their affliction they will seek him early. That is why he still tells Jeremiah in the prison, Call unto me, and I will answer thee.

precepts.text: In our affliction we will seek Him early, so in the land of our captivity He gives us a heart and ears to hear.
precepts.point: Baruch is told not to seek great things for himself, for the Most High will bring evil upon all flesh, but his life He will give him for a prey in all places wherever he goes.

note.label: Jeremiah 45: The Word of Comfort to Baruch the Scribe

precepts.why:
Baruch is told not to seek great things for himself, for the Lord will bring evil upon all flesh. Hosea shows what that evil is for: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

In our affliction we will seek him early. That is why, in the land of our captivity, he gives us a heart and ears to hear, as Baruch wrote.
